# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1517
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1517
- **Title**: gh-1510 [BUG] CLI TUI wrap eats the space at the wrap boundary — nightly subagent memory test red 2 nights (regression window 10-08→10-09)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1510` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +533
- **Deletions**: -24
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T20:41:16Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T22:34:52Z

## PR Description

Closes #1510
### Root Cause
- The eaten space was **not** the line wrapper — it was rogue `print()` output. The hosted `flutter_agent_memory` package logs debug info via bare `print()` (with `// ignore: avoid_print`) on the CLI's main isolate. In TUI mode stdout IS the terminal, so those raw bytes interleaved with the CellRenderer's frame protocol and physically clobbered/scrolled screen cells. The cell-diff grid (which assumes exclusive terminal ownership) stayed stale, so the next frame skipped repainting the "unchanged" space cell between "round-trip" and "complete". The xterm emulator drops the clobbered cell in `getText()` → screen shows `memory round-tripcomplete` → `waitForScreen` times out. Captured failing wire: `[17;1H…Fa[0m memory round-trip[17;24Hcomplete` with `TAG=…` print fragments mid-row. #1420 only shifted which cell got skipped onto the space.
- Latent wrap bug confirmed while investigating: `wrapAnsiLine('aaaa bbbb', 4)` dropped the boundary space when a word ends exactly at the wrap width, violating its own "reassembling reproduces the text" contract.

### Fix
- `lib/src/memory/memory_controller.dart`: new `printSink` — every package-facing op (`add`/`search`/`list`/`delete`/`maintain`) runs in a zone whose `ZoneSpecification.print` delegates to the sink; null sink preserves historical behavior.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`: wires `printSink` to the diagnostic log (`~/.fah/logs/fa.log`). Verified end-to-end: 0 print bytes reach the PTY; the lines land in fa.log.
- `lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart`: `wrapAnsiLine` now carries an edge-boundary space onto the continuation row (terminal autowrap) instead of dropping it; a following word that no longer fits hard-cuts across rows. `rows.join()` now reproduces the visible text exactly.

### Test Coverage
- `test/integration/subagent_integration_test.dart` (the nightly failure): **passed 3/3** locally post-fix (pre-fix it failed ~1 in 3 with the exact nightly symptom — the skipped space cell and `TAG=…` print fragments visible on the wire).
- `test/memory_print_redirect_test.dart` (new): package prints reach the sink and never stdout; null-sink pass-through pinned.
- `test/cli/ansi_markdown_test.dart`: exact-boundary REG test (`'aaaa bbbb'` w=4 → `['aaaa', ' bbb', 'b']`), trailing-space test, and a seeded property test (200 random texts × widths 3–32 → stripped row join round-trips the text, rows never overflow).
- Full suite: 6000+ tests green. 19 failures in `headless_log_file`/`yolo_rm_critical_e2e`/`headless_tools_flag`/`backend_mode_cli`/`header_badge_pty`/`browser_ext` and a native VM abort at process shutdown were each reproduced **identically on the base commit** (this runner's environment; unrelated to this change). All suites covering the changed code pass: `ansi_markdown`, `transcript_markdown_perf`, `transcript_table_render`, the `fa_tui_*` render tests, and the whole `test/memory/` suite.

### Notes
- Rows at the wrap boundary may now start with a carried space — intentional, matches real terminal autowrap; markdown is already formatted before wrapping so no block-marker interaction.
- The `hub: cannot bind 127.0.0.1:PORT` log noise from `fah_hub_serve_ports_test.dart` is unrelated (the tests pass) and untouched.

# gh-1510: [BUG] CLI TUI wrap eats the space at the wrap boundary — nightly subagent memory test red 2 nights (regression window 10-08→10-09)

## Description

## Symptom

Nightly `PTY/CLI integration + cli coverage` red **two nights in a row** (runs 37880055409, 38021029680): `test/integration/subagent_integration_test.dart: memory_add and memory_search tools are available` times out in `waitForScreen('memory round-trip complete')` (pty_harness.dart:127 → subagent_integration_test.dart:240).

**Reproduces locally**: `dart test test/integration/subagent_integration_test.dart --plain-name "memory_add and memory_search tools are available"` — fails the same way.

## Root symptom (real TUI rendering bug, not a flake)

The agent's final reply IS painted — but the raw PTY stream shows the wrap boundary **eats the separating space**:

```
[17;1H … ">_Fa memory round-trip" … [17;24H "complete"
```

Screen buffer ends up with `memory round-tripcomplete` (no space) — `waitForScreen('memory round-trip complete')` can never match. The diff renderer paints the wrapped continuation segment at the adjacent column without the space cell.

## Regression window

Nightly green 2026-10-08 03:35Z → red 2026-10-09 03:36Z. TUI-touching commit in the window: 336042cfd (gh-1415 subagent status row, #1420) — the extra live row shifts viewport layout, which either moved the wrap point onto the space or broke the diff painter's space handling. `ansi_markdown.dart`/wrapAnsiLine untouched since #828 — the space-eating is likely latent and newly exposed.

## Acceptance

1. Failing test green again (root fix, not test-weakening): wrapped assistant text must preserve whitespace at the wrap boundary in the rendered screen buffer.
2. REG: a wrap-at-space unit test at the exact boundary (word ends at last column, next word continues) in the TUI render layer.
3. Never-again: if the space-eating is latent in the diff painter, add a property-style test (random text × widths → screen buffer round-trip preserves text modulo styling).
